keyFindings.description: The half of round 5's finding that asked for the collector's own names to be reserved is not done, and the consequence is the same one the other half fixed: a run that lost evidence and passed. `session_copy` refuses an empty name, `.`, `..` and a collision between two keys, but not a name that collides with a directory the collector itself makes. A pod can write a session row keyed `<pod_sessions_dir>/controller` — the table takes arbitrary text keys (`internal/ompsessions/ompsessions.go:44-47`) — which derives to `controller` and is written as a regular file. `collect_transcripts` then runs `mkdir -p "$evidence/transcripts/controller"` and `cp -R …` unguarded at `:2560-2561`: both fail, neither clears `copied`, and `:2563` returns success. The teardown's new `if ! collect_transcripts` (`:2584`) therefore sees a success, records no `teardown_failed`, and goes on to destroy the work directory holding the operator controller's real sessions. The `session_copy` half is genuinely fixed and its refusal does reach the verdict; this is the reservation the same finding named. Reserve `controller` and `daemon-controller` in the derivation, and let the controller copy's own failures reach `copied`.

Security[sandbox], hardening: `legionClaim` refuses an operator volume naming a claim of Legion's own by three prefixes — `issue-legion-`, `cache-legion-`, `tree-legion-` — and the claim name this change introduces is none of them. An issue's disk is now the pod's own generic ephemeral volume, named `<pod>-issue`, so an operator `pod.volumes` entry naming it is accepted and projected into every role container (`manifest.go:448`), against the stated contract of the guard immediately above it. This needs the operator's own configuration, so it is not an agent's escalation and it is not blocking; the guard's own words are what make it worth closing.

The cutover tells a deployment still on the file store that it 'copies its sessions into the table first', linking to 'Copying file sessions before turning it on'. That section says plainly that only `legion-v10.0.0` can copy and that a deployment on `legion-v10.1.0` to `legion-v10.2.x` has no copy path at all — its switch is a drain at a pushed boundary with those sessions lost — and `scripts/sessions-import-pods.sh:44-50` refuses such a project by name. So the path is disclosed, not missing, and the thermonuclear reading of it as an unexecutable prerequisite overstates it. What stands is the one sentence: a reader on `v10.1.x` is told to copy and learns only by following the link that they cannot. Say it at the link.

Three texts still teach what this change removed. `docs/kubernetes.md:918-919` says `legion sessions import` and `legion sessions mark-lost` 'are unchanged', while `cmd/legion/sessions.go` has deleted `mark-lost` and the same manual records its removal at `:1011-1013`. `manifest_test.go:825` says a later pod 'runs the .venv as it is and reuses what an earlier pod downloaded', which a disk that dies with its pod makes false. `relaunch.go:497` logs `relabelling a sandbox for its issue's new tree, keeping its volume`, an operator-visible line naming a volume an issue Sandbox no longer owns.

unprovenGapJudgement.position: The framing of the remaining gap as two cluster-only behaviours, each a uid comparison, is accurate about what cannot be reached and understates what has not been exercised. Those two are acceptance 1's cluster half and acceptance 4, and nothing in this repository can reach them; that part is right. What it leaves out is that Stage 4b has run at no head at all, and this change rewrote its parked, released and lifecycle assertions, its delete log line and its whole transcript reader. Those are not behaviours we cannot reach: they are assertions whose own correctness is unverified, and the base rate on this change is that every reading of that harness found a defect — the Stage 4a marker path in round 2, two assertion families in round 2, the session reader in round 4, the exporter traversal in round 5, the unreserved collector name in this round. Five readings, five defects, no runs. An acceptance that says 'two behaviours remain provable only on a cluster' is true; one that lets a reader infer the rest is proven is not. The sentence I would want a stranger to read is that the tree-level proof is repaired but unexecuted, and that its repairs were found by reading rather than by running.
